summary: Since a 2023 presidential decree Angola waives visas for tourists from around 100 countries — including the EU, UK, US, China and Japan — for stays of up to 30 days per visit and 90 days per year. Everyone else applies for a pre-approved tourist eVisa collected on arrival, and a yellow fever certificate is required from all travelers.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Angola requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) from all travelers aged 9 months and over, whatever your departure point. It is routinely checked on arrival in Luanda.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present year-round throughout Angola, including Luanda. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Travelers' health: Angola

travelInsurance.text: No official source states an insurance requirement for tourists to Angola. Medical facilities are limited outside private clinics in Luanda, so cover that includes medical evacuation is advisable.

source.name: SME — Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (official Angola visa portal)

onwardTicket.text: eVisa applicants must upload a round-trip flight booking and an accommodation booking in Angola. Visa-free visitors may also be asked by officials at the border to show a return or onward ticket.

source.name: SME — Angola eVisa portal (evisa.ao): visa waiver and required documents

proofOfFunds.text: eVisa applicants must upload proof of financial means to cover the stay. The SME portal refers to a minimum set by law but does not publish the amount.

source.name: SME — Angola eVisa portal (evisa.ao): visa waiver and required documents

currencyLimits.text: Non-residents must declare foreign cash or travellers cheques worth USD 5,000 or more on arrival (USD 10,000 for residents) and keep the certified declaration. You cannot take out more than USD 5,000 in foreign currency (USD 10,000 for residents), plus up to AOA 50,000 in kwanzas.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Angola travel advice: entry requirements

notes: Diamonds and other minerals may not be taken out of Angola without an official license.
Photography of government buildings, ports, airports and military sites is prohibited.

payments.text: In Luanda, cards are widely used. The local Multicaixa network is everywhere and international Visa/Mastercard work at hotels, supermarkets and better restaurants. Outside the capital carry kwanzas in cash, and change money only at banks and official bureaux.

safety.text: Luanda has a high level of crime, some of it violent: avoid walking around, especially alone or after dark, and keep valuables out of sight in traffic. Roads outside the main cities can be poor, and the UK advises against all but essential travel to Cabinda Province, except Cabinda city, because separatist groups have attacked foreigners and there is a risk of kidnap.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Angola travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September — the dry, cooler cacimbo season — is the best window for Luanda, the coast and inland trips; the rains run roughly October to April.

tips.text: Visa-free entry under the 2023 decree is for tourism only — 30 days per visit and 90 days per year. Border officials may ask for a return or onward ticket, and everyone needs a yellow fever card, so keep both to hand.
Angola checks yellow fever certificates from every arriving traveler — get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and carry the ICVP card with your passport.
You can take out no more than AOA 50,000 in kwanza cash — spend or reconvert the rest before departure, and only exchange money at banks or licensed bureaux.
Little English is spoken outside upmarket Luanda. A few phrases of Portuguese, or a translation app that works offline, goes a long way.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Angola?
faq.answer: Around 100 nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, China, Japan, most of the Americas and much of Africa — have been visa-exempt for tourism since Angola's 2023 decree, for stays of up to 30 days. Everyone else applies for a pre-approved eVisa via the official SME portal or at an embassy.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Angola visa-free?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days per visit, capped at 90 days per calendar year. For longer stays you need a visa from the SME portal or an Angolan embassy, and tourist visas can generally be extended once for a further 30 days in-country.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Angola?
faq.answer: Yes — Angola requires the certificate from all travelers aged 9 months and over, regardless of where you fly from, and it is routinely checked on arrival in Luanda.

faq.question: How does the Angola eVisa work?
faq.answer: You apply online at smevisa.gov.ao and receive a pre-approval letter; SME does not publish a processing time. You board with the letter and the visa itself is stamped on arrival at Luanda or another international entry point; the fee is Kz 36,600, paid in cash at the border.

faq.question: What documents do I need at the Angolan border?
faq.answer: Everyone needs a passport valid 6 months with two blank pages and a yellow fever certificate. eVisa applicants must also show a round-trip booking, accommodation and proof of means, and border officials may ask visa-free visitors for a return or onward ticket too.
